design_goal: add a shared 'Project focus' category filter to the portfolio's own project grid — with a live result count and a filterable card grid — surfaced across the Projects, Overview and About pages, while keeping the navigation and Angular build stable
problem_statement: This is an Angular developer-portfolio site: an Overview landing page at /, a Projects page at /projects, and an About page at /about, all wrapped in a shared app shell (a top navigation bar with the wordmark and Overview / Projects / About links, and a dark footer band). The Projects page lists the owner's engineering projects as a card grid driven by local JSON. The owner wants a 'Project focus' filter to sit above that grid so visitors can narrow the projects by focus area. Build a shared Project-focus filter that (1) renders a labelled row of category tabs (All work / Platforms / ML & Data / Edge & Tooling) above the project card grid, (2) filters the grid to the chosen category and keeps a live result count readout in sync — reading 'Showing N of 6 - <category>' — so clicking the Platforms tab shows the two Platforms projects and the readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 - Platforms', (3) is surfaced not only on the Projects page but also as a shared 'Project focus' section on the Overview and About pages so the filter is a consistent portfolio feature, and (4) lays out its tab row and card grid responsively so no portfolio page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone and the cards never overlap or become illegible. Keep the rest of the site — the navigation, the existing profile and experience copy, and the Angular build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Project focus' filter component above the project card grid: a labelled tab row with All work / Platforms / ML & Data / Edge & Tooling and a live result-count readout.

Clicking a category tab must filter the card grid to that category AND update the readout to 'Showing N of 6 - <category>' (for example the Platforms tab -> 'Showing 2 of 6 - Platforms'); the readout must reflect the current selection, not a stale count captured once at load.

Surface the same shared 'Project focus' filter on the Overview (/) and About (/about) pages too, not only on the Projects page, so it is a consistent cross-page portfolio feature (a shared component, not divergent per-page copies).
The tab row and card grid must lay out responsively so no portfolio page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px) and the project cards never overlap into an illegible pile.

Style the filter in the emerald/teal portfolio language (light-green tab chips, an active chip with a green fill and readable white label, dark-ink card titles on white cards) so it reads as part of the portfolio and stays legible.
Preserve the Overview/Projects/About navigation, the existing profile and experience copy, and the Angular build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the Project-focus filter as a single shared component so one source of truth reaches the Projects page grid and the Overview / About surfaces; do not paste divergent copies per page.
Compute the result-count readout and the shown cards from the CURRENT active category on every click, so the count can never go stale relative to the highlighted tab or the filtered grid.

The tab row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) and the card grid must wrap into a responsive multi-column layout so it never forces horizontal overflow and the cards never overlap on tablet or mobile.

Adopt the emerald/teal portfolio theme (green accent, light-green tab chips, an active chip with a green fill and legible white label, dark-ink titles on white cards) so the filter reads as part of the portfolio and every label stays legible (no near-white text on near-white fills).
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the existing profile or experience copy, or the Angular build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the Overview page across viewports.
desktop_projects, mobile_projects and desktop_about protect the Projects and About pages; mobile_projects must not overflow horizontally.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home scroll the shared 'Project focus' filter into view on the Overview page and must show it without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_projects protects the Project-focus filter's presence and clean grid layout on the Projects page.
engagement_toggle_home clicks the Platforms tab on the Projects page; the readout must then read 'Showing 2 of 6 - Platforms'.

change_completion: The shared 'Project focus' filter is present above the project grid on the Projects page AND surfaced on the Overview and About pages (the shared component reaches all three routes).

After clicking the Platforms tab, the grid filters to the Platforms projects and the readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 - Platforms' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 6 of 6 - All work'.
design_consistency: The filter and its card grid match the reference's emerald/teal portfolio styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not a collapsed overlapping pile.
The filter adopts the emerald portfolio theme tokens and keeps tab and card labels legible across every page.
responsive: No captured portfolio page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tab row and card grid wrap.
desktop_rail_projects, mobile_projects and the Overview surface keep the filter grid readable across viewports without clipping, overflow or overlapping cards.
regression: Navigation (Overview/Projects/About) and the existing profile/experience copy remain present and functional.
The Angular build is not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

author_notes: slot_188 L4 hardening onto the ronald-hove Angular-Portfolio-Template repository (reassigned off the shared ByteGrad portfolio repo kept by slot_135). The Angular portfolio's remote Bootstrap, FontAwesome and analytics assets are vendored locally so every leg renders offline-clean, and the existing profile and experience copy plus the navigation shell are shared byte-identically across legs. The L4 levers ride on the portfolio's OWN project grid: a shared 'Project focus' category filter component (tab row All work / Platforms / ML & Data / Edge & Tooling, a live result-count readout, and a filterable card grid of six project cards with preview images). reference = the filter above the Projects grid AND surfaced on the Overview and About pages, a fluid wrapping tab row and multi-column card grid, emerald/teal legible styling, and a readout that recomputes from the active category (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the filter's wiring is correct so its readout updates on click (passes D4), but it is present on the Projects page only (fails D2 cross-page on the Overview/About surfaces), its tab row is a fixed-width nowrap strip so mobile /projects overflows ~249px (fails D6), and its card grid collapses into an overlapping negative-margin pile with near-white illegible tab and label text (fails D3). bad = a 'smart wrong' filter: present on the Projects page only (fails D2), the same fixed nowrap tab row (fails D6 ~249px), the same collapsed illegible overlapping grid (fails D3), and a readout snapshotted once at load with an unfiltered grid so clicking Platforms leaves it at 'Showing 6 of 6 - All work' (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The Angular build renders every route with vendored assets and no network calls. Project preview images live in src/assets/img as brand-gradient SVGs.
